take_homes: An agent can be steered by plain text in a file it reads, so the risk is what it has access to and not only what I prompt.
Giving the agent less access makes a bad answer smaller, and closing a door is the cheapest fix.
A security check can be a skill with two lenses, company policy and agent risk. I can rerun it on my other agents.

monday.move: Run the agent-audit skill on the agents my engineers already run, and look at what they can write to and what untrusted docs they read.
monday.who: me, plus one engineer who owns the agent setup
monday.when: Monday morning, probably after the standup
monday.stop_condition: I have a ranked list of risks and one I'm willing to fix. If it turns into a policy project I stop.
monday.blocker: I'd rather build the org-wide setup for sales first, and nobody has given me time to audit what we already run.

misconception.why: The audit found a path I'd considered fine because the agent is good. 'The agent is good' did not stop a poisoned document from steering it. I'm still not sure checking the output is for me, since I skipped the review step in the exercises.

one_line: The injection and 'give it less access' bits are worth it, but about a third of this module is filler, and I'd run the audit myself and skip the slides.
